issue_context.title: Shift-clicking "Add Sun to Scene" or "Add Environment to Scene" no longer adds both sun and environment at the same time
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.rc2

### System information

Fedora 37, GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA 525.85.05)

### Issue description

Prior to 4.0.beta17, you could hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> to add both the current preview sun and environment to the scene when clicking either **Add Sun to Scene** or **Add Environment to Scene** in the 3D editor's preview sky/environment editor:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/219509859-7b0cddff-ae04-43f7-b2a2-4c22e1484271.png)

This feature no longer works since 4.0.beta17. If I hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while clicking, it acts as if it wasn't holding <kbd>Shift</kbd> and will only add the sun or environment (which matches whichever button I clicked).

This feature is useful to add both sun and environment with a single click, speeding up the setup of simple test projects (useful for MRPs and prototyping).

I bisected the regression to 9f426498231816ccb9d686b3944373f61312aa24. cc @bruvzg

### Steps to reproduce

- Ensure the preview sun and sky are enabled, so you can edit them and add them to the current scene. Also make sure there is neither a WorldEnvironment nor a DirectionalLight3D node in the current scene.
- Click the 3 vertical dots icon at the top of the 3D editor viewport, next to the globe.
- Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> and click **Add Sun to Scene** or **Add Environment to Scene**.
- Notice it only adds one node, while it's supposed to add both. Test this in previous 4.0 betas for comparison.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A

I came by this issue as just clicking the buttons didn't work at all for me in Godot 4.1.1 on macOS 10.13.
Getting desperate I finally double clicked.
Then I found double clicking with shift worked as expected for me.

I can still reproduce this on 4.3.dev 51991e201 on my end (Linux). Double-clicking doesn't work on my end as the dialog closes before I can perform the second click.

@ryevdokimov Which OS are you using?
That's odd, I quickly glanced at the code and didn't see anything wrong or specific to an OS. I'm on Windows 11 Build 10.0.22631. I can check again.
What if we replace it outright with a button right in the middle to add both? More accessible?

> What if we replace it outright with a button right in the middle to add both? More accessible?

That could work too, as long as we can fit all 3 buttons without making the UI too large.

Is a button smacked right into the middle like this possible? Or would it require too much fiddling with Control nodes?
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/66727710/21cb2071-b69c-43b9-97ca-98af67143477)

> Is a button smacked right into the middle like this possible? Or would it require too much fiddling with Control nodes?

That was my initial thought, but it might look confusing. In terms of implementation, it should be a metter of moving the buttons out of the columns and into an HBoxContainer as the last item of a VBoxContainer with the SplitContainer on top.
Then it could be called "Add Both" instead of showing the symbol?

Sounds good :slightly_smiling_face:

On Windows I can hold down shift and then click on button.
